entries.defect: [B1] Proposal: gate only an author-declared final pushed SHA and rerun every check invalidated by subsequent changes, while retaining unaffected valid results; basis: 1415 had nine same-SHA repeats and 1432 had four, alongside repeated fix and sync rounds; expected gain: fewer redundant acceptance runs, amount not measurable from the material; risk: incorrectly treating a changed dependency or environment as unaffected; decide by auditing retained evidence against final SHAs and comparing suite durations, reds, acceptance time and landed points/hour with the current policy.

[B2] Proposal: enforce the existing diagnosis stop after one repeat of an unchanged SHA, section, backend and failure signature, reopening execution only after a relevant commit or recorded environmental change; basis: 73% of finished suite minutes were red and thirteen same-SHA repeats are identified on 1432 and 1415; expected gain: avoid unproductive retries, but the avoidable fraction is not measurable from the material; risk: stopping investigation rather than stopping repetition; decide by measuring repeat counts, diagnosis-to-fix time, final local suite results and landed points/hour.

[B3] Proposal: reuse an existing main comparison only where the red is already charged to an open point and main remains unchanged in the relevant section; basis: acceptance includes main comparison runs on 1414 and 1418 and substantial red-run time; expected gain: eliminate eligible repeated comparisons, count not measurable from the material; risk: misclassifying a new regression as an existing red; decide by checking section and dependency changes, baseline provenance, new uncharged reds, comparison minutes and landed points/hour.

[B4] Proposal: diagnose STALLED runs promptly and resolve confirmed abandoned suite or run-wait processes before retrying, using existing controls; basis: five hung 1442 runs consumed about 4.3 inferred hours and overlapping-suite logs identified a leftover run-wait process; expected gain: recover some hang and contention time, not necessarily all 4.3 hours; risk: terminating a legitimate long run or leaving its browser alive; decide by measuring hung duration, surviving processes, quiet-host versus subsequent suite durations and reds, and landed points/hour.

[B5] Proposal: consistently replace the 45-minute default wait with the existing measured suite plan and resume work when completion is observed; basis: suite durations range from short section runs to approximately 43-minute full backend runs, and a separate 35-minute idle stretch occurred; expected gain: reduce oversleep, although the material does not establish that oversleep caused that stretch; risk: excessive wake-ups increasing bookkeeping; decide by measuring suite completion-to-owner-resumption delay, wake-up overhead per point, suite duration and landed points/hour.

[B6] Proposal: send each fix to one authoring destination, consolidate already-known findings into that request where possible, and keep picture-fix loops local; basis: 1417 received simultaneous local and cloud requests for the same fix, wasting 17.4 local-agent minutes and 181,408 tokens without landing local work; expected gain: no observed critical-path gain from that incident, with possible contention savings not measurable from the material; risk: delaying a fix if the selected author stalls; decide by measuring duplicate authoring, handover latency, host memory, suite durations and reds, bookkeeping and landed points/hour.

[B7] Proposal: execute the existing one-cloud-author overlap promptly when acceptance opens, or during eligible routine boundary bookkeeping when the queue choice is already valid, carrying the author in the successor declaration; basis: authoring took 7.1 hours against 33.3 acceptance hours, and freeing slots alone previously commissioned nothing; expected gain: hide authoring and avoidable commissioning delay behind existing owner work, amount not measurable from the material; risk: stale queue selection, lost handover or excess finished work; decide by measuring submission timing, actual overlap, acceptance starvation, suite durations, memory, reds, finished-branch ages, bookkeeping and landed points/hour, retaining all current bounds and front-order priority.

entries.file: runbook-throughput.md, lightweight work during suite waits
entries.defect: [B8] Proposal: overlap the existing cross-vendor review and preparation with suite waits on the final SHA through a lightweight or remote path; basis: acceptance dominates elapsed phase time and the runbook already permits early review, but review durations are unlogged; expected gain: overlap review latency, not measurable from the material; risk: reviewing superseded code or introducing local load; decide by measuring review-to-suite overlap, re-review work, peak memory, paired quiet/load suite durations and reds, bookkeeping and landed points/hour, rejecting any measurable suite slowdown or load-induced red.

entries.file: runbook-throughput.md, final-SHA acceptance and main sync
entries.defect: [B9] Proposal: perform required main synchronization and consolidate known fixes before declaring the branch final and starting expensive gates, repeating affected checks after any later change; basis: twelve syncs cost approximately 3.8 inferred hours and 1417 incurred two syncs with about 1.4 inferred hours; expected gain: fewer superseded gates, with no evidence that all sync time is removable; risk: postponing necessary synchronization or using stale evidence; decide by measuring sync-induced invalidations, superseded suite minutes, branch age, final-SHA quality and landed points/hour.

[B10] Proposal: apply the existing single bookkeeping commit per boundary and remove duplicate retrospective, guide-attest and queue-refresh work, preserving publication receipts at their required time; basis: ordinary post-landing gaps were 0.15–0.5 hours, with several larger gaps containing other work; expected gain: reduce the removable bookkeeping component, not the entire gap; risk: stale queue order or incomplete successor context; decide by measuring active bookkeeping time per point, commission delay, receipt timing, handover completeness and landed points/hour, rejecting any increase in bookkeeping or setback to front-ranked orders.

[B11] Proposal: switch off the existing fill-to-three demand while retaining POOL_CAP=3 as the branch ceiling and preserving commission-guard, rather than repeatedly manufacturing work or explanations for unused slots; basis: the code describes three as a target while the current runbook explicitly makes it only a ceiling, and observed cloud work waited for acceptance; expected gain: less commissioning and justification overhead, not measurable separately; risk: overlooking genuine acceptance starvation; decide by measuring free-slot explanations, bookkeeping per point, ready-successor starvation, finished-branch age and landed points/hour without increasing author or heavy-job bounds.

[B12] Proposal: when cloud authoring is unavailable or approaching credit expiry, trial one local author alongside one browser suite, changing only the blanket local-author prohibition and retaining one browser/picture job; basis: authoring is shorter than acceptance, but author-plus-suite performance was not isolated in the material; expected gain: potentially hide local authoring after cloud availability ends, not measurable from the material; risk: CPU, memory or GPU contention and new reds; decide with repeated same-SHA quiet/load suite comparisons, peak host/process memory, red rate, bookkeeping, branch waits and matched-workload landed points/hour, rejecting any measurable suite slowdown, load-induced red or throughput regression.

[B13] Proposal: separately trial overlapping an already-required CPU-only gate with one browser suite, retaining both-backend checks and the mandatory post-merge gate; basis: suites dominate acceptance, but CPU-gate duration and contention are not separately measured; expected gain: possible acceptance overlap, not measurable from the material; risk: browser slowdown, memory pressure or timing failures; decide by measuring both jobs’ durations against quiet-host runs on the same SHA, peak memory, reds and landed points/hour, adopting only if suites remain unchanged and throughput improves against the current-policy control.

entries.file: existing autostart takeover, boundary ownership fence, runbook-throughput.md
entries.defect: [B14] Proposal: retune or switch off the existing pid-reused takeover path until predecessor exit is established through the existing ownership mechanism, preserving normal successor launches at every boundary; implementation details are not attached; basis: a false inactivity decision launched a second owner while the first still wrote, costing about 0.4 inferred hours; expected gain: avoid that class of lost work and context; risk: delayed recovery of a genuinely dead owner; decide by replaying the recorded decision case and observing real boundary recovery, owner overlap, recovery latency, superseded suite minutes and landed points/hour without introducing a new guard.

[B15] Finding: the binding comparison is 3.42 hours per landed point excluding host-down time, approximately 0.292 landed points/hour; its source window contained 25 distinct landed points over 99.0 raw hours and excluded 13.6 host-down hours.

[B16] Finding: the inventory window landed twenty points in 70.5 hours, giving 3.52 raw hours/point and 2.86 hours/point after excluding its 13.4-hour host outage; this is a different window from the baseline and its outage estimate differs by 0.2 hours.

[B17] Finding: nine post-1444 points landed in 22.8 hours, approximately 2.53 hours/point, already below the 3.42-hour baseline as an observation; attribution to the bounds is not measurable because the window is short, work overlaps and only four points are game-class, including diagnostic point 1415.

[B18] Finding: the reported 5.69 hours per game point divides the whole post-1444 window by its four game points; it is not measured average game-point acceptance time, and a matching pre-1443 game-only throughput baseline is not supplied.

[B19] Finding: the prescribed cycle ends after both five landed points and 48 hours have been reached; the attached post-1444 observation reaches nine points but only 22.8 hours, so it does not establish completion of that cycle.

[B20] Finding: acceptance totals 33.3 phase hours versus 7.1 authoring and 3.2 landing hours; these are phase estimates rather than a directly instrumented utilization partition, and authoring, acceptance and waiting can overlap.

[B21] Finding: cloud handovers took approximately 0.1–1.1 hours while post-1444 game acceptance took 0.75–5.1 hours; finished cloud branches waited approximately 3.6 hours on 1388, 2.5 on 1418 and 1.4 on 1417, indicating acceptance pressure rather than demonstrated author scarcity.

[B22] Finding: current provisional bounds are one submitted/running cloud author, one finished branch waiting, three open branches as a ceiling, one local heavy job and daemon off; increasing cloud concurrency requires observed acceptance starvation for a ready successor and no finished branch waiting over a day, neither of which is established here.

[B23] Finding: old branches waited roughly 35–47 hours inside the window and some existed for days beforehand; their waits overlap each other and host downtime, so they cannot be summed into recoverable batch time, and parking a finished branch would not satisfy the binding one-day wait limit.

[B24] Finding: cloud submission precedes branch creation, so branch-based commission-guard cannot enforce the submitted-cloud bound; the existing in-flight declaration must carry all concurrent jobs and evidence because a new waiting-on declaration replaces the previous record.

[B25] Finding: branch occupancy includes unmerged local and remote feat branches minus valid parks; new assignments to parked branches reoccupy slots immediately, and assignments adding no branch may continue even when the pool is full; branch occupancy is not the same quantity as active authoring processes.

[B26] Finding: unreadable branch or record evidence deliberately permits commissioning with a notice, and an unreadable parked tip can remain parked; therefore the guard’s cap and queue decisions are not unconditional guarantees when evidence is unreadable.

[B27] Finding: DAEMON_POOL_CAP counts running, checkpointing, stalled and unknown attempt states, while ready-for-review and landing free a slot; a daemon author cap of one would therefore still allow another author after a finished branch queues, violating the runbook’s no-refill-while-a-finished-branch-waits rule unless existing behavior already handles that condition, which is not shown.

[B28] Finding: a test asserts that DAEMON_POOL_CAP and POOL_CAP agree, while the runbook suggests lowering the daemon cap before enabling it and retaining branch cap three; lowering only the daemon constant is not demonstrated to be a complete valid change, and daemon-on throughput under the desired bounds is not measurable.

[B29] Finding: 1347 previously occupied one slot for 45.6 hours within the window but is now parked at an unchanged tip, with open=[] and slotsFree=3; its remaining worktree is 626 commits behind main, but current CPU, memory, GPU usage and finished status are not measurable from its existence.

[B30] Finding: independence checks only named file or directory overlap against supplied runningFiles, excluding gated and unnamed specifications; it does not establish dependency, semantic, CPU, memory or GPU independence, and the excerpt does not establish which complete running-file set callers supply.

[B31] Finding: POOL_CAP also determines the number of workable front candidates, so changing it changes commissioning eligibility as well as occupancy; user-gated points remain blocked even when already in flight or carrying an override, and permission to choose among three candidates does not prove that a choice leaves front-ranked orders unaffected.

[B32] Finding: the reported 85 runs comprise 28 green, twelve partial, forty red and five hung; finished runs consumed 15.8 hours, including 11.5 red hours, so approximately 73% of finished suite time was red rather than evidence that all that time was avoidable.

[B33] Finding: eleven full polish-villagers runs consumed 8.1 hours with a median near 43 minutes per backend; retaining both backends makes one complete pair roughly 86 minutes at that median before retries, so two-backend cost cannot be removed by counting a cloud green.

[B34] Finding: the 23.10 overlap involved two authors’ suites sharing one GPU and machine-under-load warnings; the timed-out whole-water-errand check was unique to overlap, but jar-take and pointing failures recurred on solo runs of the same SHA, preventing attribution of all those reds to load.

[B35] Finding: the runbook reports load moving suite duration by about one fifth, but attached paired quiet/load timing distributions, CPU-only overlap results, peak memory and safe capacity margins are not supplied; no positive concurrency setting is established by those statements.

[B36] Finding: four same-SHA repeats are identified on 1432 and nine on 1415, but identical SHA alone does not establish duplicate section, backend, failure signature or unchanged environment; exact avoidable retry time is not measurable.

[B37] Finding: twelve syncs cost approximately 3.8 inferred hours, with some acceptance-opening sync costs inseparable; required re-gating after a changed SHA is not redundant merely because a previous SHA was tested.

[B38] Finding: landing consumed approximately 3.2 hours overall and usually eight minutes per point, dominated by the post-merge fast gate; the inventory reports it was never the critical path, providing no measured case for parallel landing or removing that gate.

[B39] Finding: ordinary gaps were 0.15–0.5 hours, with larger 1.0–3.1-hour gaps; at least one included main-based dress investigations, so all elapsed gap time cannot be classified as removable bookkeeping and active bookkeeping cost is not separately measured.

[B40] Finding: the window contains a 13.4-hour host outage, about 4.3 inferred hung WebGPU hours and three reported outside-outage idle stretches of 47, 54 and 35 minutes; eliminating host downtime improves calendar throughput but cannot itself improve a metric that excludes host downtime.

[B41] Finding: every one of 27,709 report intervals is contradictory-evidence involving sequence items 66 and 67, placing the whole 70.92-hour report under unknown; those class totals cannot identify the bottleneck or validate a changed policy.

[B42] Finding: owner-lock time, tool-call time, verification records, leases and no-work-evidence durations overlap; 17.91 hours without work evidence is not established idle time, and long main-commit gaps include host downtime and active acceptance.

[B43] Finding: false pid-reused takeover caused live owner overlap and about 0.4 inferred hours of lost work/context; the later 84-minute backend rerun was required for a new SHA and was expressly excluded from that loss estimate.

[B44] Finding: the duplicate local fix used 181,408 tokens, seventy tool calls and 17.4 minutes before its push was rejected; its measured critical-path cost was zero because cloud finished first, so token savings cannot be reported as measured landed-throughput gain.

[B45] Finding: 1418 omitted a local pre-merge build/lint/unit layer, used two cloud gate results and ran the mandatory local post-merge fast gate; it also ran local collision and adult-errands suites, so this record does not establish cloud substitution for a local browser suite, and pre-merge CPU-gate execution was not uniform.

[B46] Finding: phase estimates mostly come from commits, mtimes and session spans; review durations are unlogged, local author fixes are folded into acceptance and some landing logs are absent; exact review, repair, handover and bookkeeping savings are not measurable from the material.

[B47] Finding: as printed, per-point run counts total 82 and the two explicit additional main runs bring the allocation to 84 rather than the reported 85; one run is not allocated by those rows, requiring reconciliation before exact saved-run accounting.

[B48] Finding: cloud-start logs identify cloud authoring for 1415, 1388, 1416 and 1417 in addition to the brief’s 1433, 1451 and 1418; location comparisons must follow actual execution evidence rather than the brief’s incomplete list.

[B49] Finding: cloud credit expires 05.11.2026 and commissions must fit local landing capacity before expiry; remaining credit balance, exact expiry instant and post-expiry local-author throughput are not measurable, so expanding cloud work cannot be assumed to create durable capacity.

[B50] Finding: each load-adding variant requires real-load suite duration, memory, red-rate and landed-throughput measurements against quiet-host quality measurements and a matched current-policy control; use existing logs and cycle notes without new ledger fields, count completed main landings, account for workload mix and beginning/end backlog, exclude host downtime consistently, preserve one owner, serial landing, front-order priority and finished waits within one day, and reject adoption if quality slows, bookkeeping rises or throughput does not improve; the material supplies no statistical threshold or sample size establishing such acceptance.
